p:cNvPr.descr: A diagram showing the processes and results of quantitative PCR. (a) A diagram showing an overview of the PCR process. The diagram begins at the top with a probe (labeled top left), which is a blue hairpin-shaped line with small blue lines on the inside, perpendicular to the main structure. There is a green glowing ball on the left end of the hairpin; it is labeled the fluorophore. There is a purple ball on the right end of the hairpin labeled the quenching molecule. There is a gray text box to the right reading, “Fluorophore signal is quenched when the probe forms a semistable hairpin.” Below is a down arrow with a text box to the left reading, “Probe binds preferentially to target DNA; fluorophore is separated from the quenching molecule, and the fluorescence signal increases.” Below is a light blue strand of target DNA, labeled below, which is simply a light blue bar with short perpendicular light blue lines coming upward off it. The probe, which is dark blue, lines up with a section of DNA just above it, preparing to bind. The fluorophore-bonded end is connected to the DNA; the quenching molecule end is sticking up and to the right, not yet bonded. (b) A graph shows the results of a quantitative PCR. The vertical axis is labeled “signal (arbitrary units)” with a range of 0 to 2 and interval 1. The horizontal axis is labeled “PCR cycle number” and has range 0 to 40 with interval 20. Just above 0 on the vertical axis is a dashed horizontal line labeled “threshold.” The first curve on the graph is black and is below the threshold line, barely rising or curving at all. It is labeled the baseline on the left and is labeled “no template” on the right end. Above this, there are three curves that follow a similar path. The leftmost curve is light green and crosses the threshold line at approximately the 15th PCR cycle. It flattens out at about 38 PCR cycles, just below the 2 signal. This is sample 1, labeled at the top. The curve to the right of this is almost identical in shape, but instead is darker green and crosses the threshold line at approximately the 20th PCR cycle. This is sample 2 labeled at the top. To the right is sample 3, labeled above. It is the same general shape but crosses the threshold line at approximately the 25th PCR cycle. It is dark green. The portions of the curves which steeply rise are bracketed and labeled on the right “exponential phase”; the area where the curves flatten out at the top is labeled the “plateau.”
